statement.p: Let \mbox{div }\vec F = 6(6-x) and 0\le a, b, c\le 14.
(a) Find the flux of \vec F out of the rectangular solid 0\le x\le a, 0\le y\le b, 0\le z\le c.
(b) For what values of a, b, c is the flux largest?

static.solution:
(a) By the Divergence Theorem, if S is the surface of the rectangular solid W, \mbox{flux }=\int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A=\int_W \mbox{div }{\vec F}\,dV = \int_0^{c}\int_0^{b}\int_0^a 6(6-x)\,dx\,dy\,dz =\int_0^{c}\int_0^{b}36 x - 3 x^2\bigg|_0^a\,dy\,dz = cb(36 a - 3 a^2).
(b) To maximize the flux 3\,abc(12 - a), we take b and c to be as large as possible and choose a to maximize (12 a - a^2) on the interval 0\le a\le 14. Thus we take a=6, b=c=14.
(c) The maximum flux is \mbox{flux }= 3\,abc(12 - a) = 21168.
